description: Orchestrator iteration 21 - brief the 11 ORPHAN_BLOCK rows unblocked in cycle 2 by the reference-chain owner BFS (re/orchestrator/ORPHAN_GATE_RESOLUTION.md). Each now has a C2+ owner and is caller-gate-evaluable for the first time. Split into two units by size so neither exceeds the worker timeout. Read-only: plates + hooks.csv + re/frida/ARG_TYPES.md only. account2 has NO Ghidra MCP, so anything needing disassembly must be reported NEEDS_GHIDRA, never guessed.

units.prompt:
READ-ONLY. NO-GUESSING: report only what a file literally shows, cite the file and line for every claim, and never infer intent. Never use 'probably', 'likely', 'appears to'. Do not write any file.

CONTEXT you should read first (both are short):
- re/orchestrator/ORPHAN_GATE_RESOLUTION.md - why these rows were ungateable and how an owner was established.
- re/frida/ARG_TYPES.md - the CURRENT inventory of A/B handlers. This is the authoritative list.

These 6 C2 rows were just unblocked. Each is listed as `rva (size bytes) -> owner(confidence)`; the owner is a reference-chain witness, NOT a function_callers edge:
0x004b6b00 (3) -> 004b6640:C2
0x00407580 (17) -> 00459000:C2
0x00471430 (22) -> 00426340,0045bae0,0047a020,0047a0f0,0047a130 (all C2)
0x0047cde0 (27) -> 0045bba0:C2
0x005b1160 (29) -> 005b74c0:C2, 005bce80:C2
0x005bfb90 (30) -> 005be260:C2

For EACH of the 6, in this order:
1. Glob for an analysis plate under re/analysis/**/ matching the RVA (try BOTH 0x-prefixed and bare 8-hex forms, e.g. 0x004b6b00.md and 004b6b00.md). If none exists, say NO_PLATE and continue - do not invent one.
2. If a plate exists, read its frontmatter and its mechanical-description section only. Report: signature as the plate states it, every global it reads, every global it writes, and every callee.
3. Grep hooks.csv for the row (RVA is 8 hex digits, no 0x, at line start) and report its current name, subsystem, confidence and notes field verbatim if under 400 chars, else summarised with the parts about signature and gating quoted exactly.
4. Classify into EXACTLY ONE of:
   - READY: plate states a complete signature, the function writes NO globals and no heap addresses, and an EXISTING handler in re/frida/ARG_TYPES.md covers its argument shape. Name that handler and quote the ARG_TYPES.md line.
   - MUTATOR_LANE: it writes any global or any memory the caller owns. Cite the exact global(s).
   - NEEDS_GHIDRA: the plate is missing, or is silent on the signature, or the signature question needs raw disassembly (x87 arguments are INVISIBLE to the decompiler, so any function touching floats where the plate shows no explicit float setup is NEEDS_GHIDRA, not READY).
   - NEEDS_NEW_HANDLER: signature is known and complete but NO handler in ARG_TYPES.md fits. You must first list which handlers you considered and say why each fails. Treat this verdict as a LAST RESORT - four consecutive prior runs proposed a new handler that already existed.
5. If READY, propose 4+ test vectors that are NON-DEGENERATE: state, for each pair, the concrete reason the two produce DIFFERENT observable outputs. A vector set where all inputs differ but all outputs collide is worthless - say so explicitly if you cannot find distinguishing vectors.

OUTPUT: one section per RVA, then a final tally line 'N READY / N MUTATOR_LANE / N NEEDS_GHIDRA / N NEEDS_NEW_HANDLER'. Be terse; this is consumed by an orchestrator, not a human reader.
